item.title: Community fork enables local execution of Japanese Government AI GenAI
item.description:
Community fork enables local execution of Japanese Government AI GenAI

A community-driven project has forked the Japanese Digital Agency’s open-source Government AI “GenAI” (Genai) to enable full local operation using local Large Language Models (LLMs) with an OpenAI-compatible API. This unofficial fork addresses the original system’s dependency on cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) by replacing those dependencies with local or open-source alternatives, allowing the software to run in closed network environments such as LGWAN.

🧩 How it works

The project modifies the Digital Agency’s genai-web repository (MIT License) to function in a local environment. To facilitate merging with upstream changes, the majority of modifications are concentrated in the OpenGENAI layer (backend/ and external apps), while the genai-web UI is kept largely unmodified to preserve the original user experience. The original genai-ai-api is not included in the fork; users must obtain it separately from the Digital Agency’s repository if needed.

⚙️ Key details

The fork currently stands at version v0.13.0. Key technical and functional features include:

  • Hardware Flexibility: Compatible with macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux systems with NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA DGX Spark).
  • Security & Deployment: Production builds use docker-compose.prod.yml with TLS termination on port 443. Closed-network verification uses docker-compose.verify.yml with HTTP on port 80.
  • Storage: Uses SeaweedFS (port 8333), which is not exposed to the host in production. Artifact downloads are handled via a reverse proxy through S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT.
  • Core Capabilities: Includes structured RAG, MCP integration, OCR, skills, Web SSH, and PII detection.

📋 Version History

Version Key Developments
v0.13.0 Training, procedure document/audit, and scheduling wizard
v0.12.0 Two-week work, draw.io editing, image generation chat, and per-building model control
v0.11.0 Multi-tenancy, recommended apps, and Markdown editor HTML/PPTX export
v0.10.0 Notebook features (research/organization), Web SSH, and app display editing
v0.9.0 Third implementation wave: Markdown editor and document creation with pluggable generation APIs
v0.8.0 Second implementation wave: Online forms, procedure bundles, application reception, and MCP
v0.7.0 First implementation wave: Document reading/checking, scheduling, and Excel generation
v0.6.0 PII detection, knowledge base pages, large attachment mapreduce, and Dify error classification
v0.5.0 Production static build deployment, multi-model swapping, and SAML authentication hardening
v0.4.0 Structured RAG, knowledge MCP, Dify integration examples, and My Number checking

💡 Why it matters

The project is explicitly an unofficial fork with no relationship to or approval from the Digital Agency. While early releases focused on replacing cloud dependencies with local/OSS components, the project’s philosophy has expanded to support actual municipal usage in closed networks. This allows local governments and organizations to utilize GenAI capabilities for administrative tasks (such as document processing and scheduling) without relying on external cloud services.

#OpenSource #LocalAI #JapanGov #LLM #Docker #RAG

Source: hirokawaguchi/open-genai

item.title: EleutherAI releases GPT-NeoX 2.0 for large-scale language model training
item.description:
EleutherAI releases GPT-NeoX 2.0 for large-scale language model training

EleutherAI has announced version 2.0 of the GPT‑NeoX library, a framework for training massive autoregressive language models on GPU clusters. The update moves the codebase onto the latest DeepSpeed release and adds versioned releases for backward compatibility.

🔍 Overview

  • Implementation of model‑parallel autoregressive transformers on GPUs.
  • Built on NVIDIA’s Megatron Language Model and augmented with DeepSpeed techniques and novel optimizations.
  • Repository records EleutherAI’s library for training large‑scale language models on GPUs.

🧩 How it works

  • Employs model parallelism to distribute transformer layers across multiple GPUs.
  • Supports launch via Slurm, MPI, and the IBM Job Step Manager.
  • Executed at scale on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs on platforms such as AWS, CoreWeave, ORNL Summit, ORNL Frontier, LUMI, and CINECA Leonardo.

⚙️ Key details

  • Two versioned releases are provided:
    • Version 2.0 – built on the latest upstream DeepSpeed and maintained going forward.
    • Version 1.0 – snapshots of the older stack used for GPT‑NeoX‑20B and the Pythia Suite.
  • Prior to 3/9/2023, GPT‑NeoX relied on DeeperSpeed, which was based on DeepSpeed 0.3.15.
  • Leverages many of the same features as the Megatron‑DeepSpeed library but with increased usability and novel optimizations.
  • Not intended for generic inference; for inference‑only needs, Hugging Face transformers is recommended.

🚀 Availability & Adoption

  • More than 40 organizations in academia, industry, and government have used GPT‑NeoX to train over 50 models.
  • Notable model families include:
    • Pythia (EleutherAI)
    • StableLM (Stability AI)
    • RedPajama‑INCITE (Together.ai)
    • FORGE (Oak Ridge National Lab)
    • Sarashina1 (SB Intuitions)
    • TildeOpen‑30B (Tilde)
  • Evo 2 from the Arc Institute was trained with Savanna, a framework derived from GPT‑NeoX.
  • A full list of models and publications is maintained in USERS.md.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a centralized, accessible location for techniques that train large‑scale autoregressive language models.
  • Accelerates research into large‑scale training by offering a usable, versioned codebase and support for diverse HPC environments.

#GPTNeoX #EleutherAI #DeepSpeed #LargeScaleTraining

Source: EleutherAI/gpt-neox

item.title: New borscht Framework Releases 12 Progressive AI Models
item.description:
New borscht Framework Releases 12 Progressive AI Models

The SITP.ai repository now hosts the borscht teaching deep learning framework, providing a progression of twelve models from a simple bigram to post‑trained transformers.

🔍 Overview

  • The repository hosts the https://sitp.ai textbook and the borscht teaching deep learning framework.
  • It includes a series of models labeled Model 1 through Model 12.

🧩 Model Progression

Model Type
Model 1 Bigram
Model 2 Discriminative Perceptron
Model 3 Probabilistic Perceptron
Model 4 Multilayer Peceptron
Model 5 Convolutional Neural Network
Model 6 Recurrent Neural Network
Model 7 Long Short-Term Memory Network
Model 8 Encoder-Decoder Pre-trained Transformers (BERT)
Model 9 Decoder Only Pre-trained Transformers (mingpt)
Model 10 Decoder Only Pre-trained Transformers (nanogpt)
Model 11 Post-trained Transformer (nanochat)
Model 12 Post-trained Transformer (nanoreasoner)

⚙️ Technical Details

  • Setup: Run borscht/setup.sh to install Python and Rust toolchains.
  • File 3B: From Managed Python to Native Rust – see pyproject.toml / Cargo.toml.
  • File 3C: From Rust to RISC‑V – see kernelscpu.rs.
  • File 4A: From Rust to CUDA Rust.
  • File 4B: Accelerate Tensor on GPU – python/borscht/tensor_nativegpu.py, rust/kernelsgpu.rs.
  • File 5: Abstracting Acceleration with Dispatcher, Storage, Allocator – see borscht/python/borscht/tensor.py.
  • File 9: From Volta to Ampere (sm80).
  • File 10: From Ampere (sm80) to Hopper (sm90).
  • File 11: Hello Tensor Compiler.
  • File 12: Hello Inference Engine.

📄 Licensing

  • The project is licensed under the June 9 Researcher Reciprocity License, adapting the Open RAIL‑S structure.
  • The license restricts using the code to train, fine‑tune, distill, generate synthetic data, embed for training, or otherwise improve an AI model or service without researcher reciprocity.
  • Contributors and authorized researchers retain rights to generate outputs, evaluate models, benchmark, publish research, and explore ideas on equal terms to ordinary users.

🚀 Next Steps

  • After Model 12, the authors suggest reading the research blog series From SITP to SOTA:
    • FS2S Part 1 (ARCH/OPT): From modded‑nanogpt to dsv3 and k3.
    • FS2S Part 1 (SYS): From Hopper to Blackwell and Rubin.
    • FS2S Part 2 (DISTSYS): From FSDP to MP.

item.title: Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models
item.description:
Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models

Solar is an open framework for interactive world models that spans open data, scalable training, long-horizon video generation, and real-time deployment. The repository contains code for two primary components: SolarWM and SolarRenderer.

🧩 How it works

The framework is built around two distinct modules that handle different aspects of video generation and rendering:

Component Function
SolarWM Enables real-time interaction, continuous exploration, and diverse generated worlds.
SolarRenderer Performs four-step, structure-conditioned video rendering with bidirectional and block-causal training and inference on MiniMax-H3.

⚙️ Key details

Several specific model releases and optimizations are included in the Solar framework:

  • SolarWM-H3 Memory: Improves long-term scene consistency and preserves visual details across revisits. Weights are available for the 33B model.
  • SolarWM-H3 Realtime: Enables low-latency interactive video generation from an image and a prompt, featuring real-time camera control.
  • H3 Streaming VAE Decoder: Allows for low-latency streaming video decoding that produces frames as latents arrive. It supports both the official MiniMax-H3 VAE and NVIDIA’s distilled StreamRender-H3 decoder.
  • Training Efficiency: Training for SolarWM-H3 is speeded up by 1.9–2.1× across Stage0.5, Stage1, and Stage2 with matching training trajectories, attributed to ResearchBoost-Agent.
  • Data: The SolarWM dataset and SolarRenderer dataset are hosted on Hugging Face.

🚀 Availability

  • Code: SolarWM and SolarRenderer code is available in the repository. Real-time deployment for SolarWM and the H3 Streaming VAE Decoder code are located in the deploy/solar_wm/ directory.
  • Weights: Model weights for both SolarWM and SolarRenderer are available on Hugging Face.
  • Demonstrations: An online demo for SolarRenderer is available on Hugging Face Spaces.
  • Documentation: Specific documentation for SolarWM is found in docs/solar_wm/ and for SolarRenderer in docs/solar_renderer/.

item.title: Strix AI: Autonomous Open‑Source Pentesting Tool

Strix AI: Autonomous Open‑Source Pentesting Tool

Strix is an open‑source AI pentesting tool that automates vulnerability discovery and repair.

🔍 Overview

  • Autonomous AI hackers that find and fix app vulnerabilities.
  • Full pentesting toolkit: reconnaissance, exploitation, and validation out of the box.
  • Real exploit validation with working PoCs, not false positives.
  • Developer‑first CLI with actionable findings and remediation guidance.
  • Auto‑fix and compliance‑ready pentest reports.

🧩 How it works

  • Multi‑agent orchestration: teams of AI pentesters collaborate and scale.
  • Runs your code dynamically, finding vulnerabilities and validating them with PoCs.
  • First run pulls a sandbox Docker image; results saved to strix_runs/<run-name>.
  • Can be run in CI/CD pipelines to block vulnerabilities before production.
  • Supports self‑update via strix --update with the appropriate upgrade command.

⚙️ Key details

  • Detects and validates critical vulnerabilities in applications.
  • Gets penetration tests done in hours, not weeks, with compliance reports.
  • Automates bug bounty research and generates PoCs for faster reporting.

🚀 Availability

  • Open source: free, runs locally with Docker and your own LLM key. Quick Start

💡 Why it matters

  • Fast, accurate security testing without manual overhead or false positives.
  • Enables developers and security teams to focus on remediation, not discovery.
  • Provides compliance‑ready reports and automated patch generation.

item.title: LLaVA-OneVision-2.5-4B-Instruct Released with Unified Video and Streaming Support
item.description:
LLaVA-OneVision-2.5-4B-Instruct Released with Unified Video and Streaming Support

🔍 Overview

On November 18, 2026, LLaVA-OneVision-2.5-4B-Instruct was released as the latest entry in the LLaVA-OneVision family. This release is a 4B model designed for single-image, multi-image, and video input that is also trained for streaming video. The release includes the training code alongside the model weights.

🧩 How it works

The model architecture supports two distinct video processing modes:

  • Long video: Enables multi-frame reasoning with efficient codec-aligned inference.
  • Streaming video: Frames arrive one at a time, and the model decides at every step whether to stay silent or speak.

The same weights and the same chat template serve both offline and streaming modes. Additionally, the model supports 3D-aware spatial reasoning, including depth, layout, and object relations. The design operates at native resolution without task-specific adapters.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model Size: 4B parameters.
  • Input Modalities: Single-image, multi-image, video, and 3D spatial data.
  • Training Efficiency: A tool named ResearchBoost-Agent made LLaVA-OneVision-2-4B SFT 2.2–3.0× faster.
  • Context: The underlying OneVision-Encoder uses HEVC-style vision transformers that add a codec-stream input mode. This approach selects motion- and residual-rich patches, allowing for dramatically longer temporal coverage under the same token budget compared to prior ViT backbones.

📦 Datasets

Four datasets ship with the LLaVA-OneVision family, including two new ones for LLaVA-OneVision-2 and two carried forward from 1.5:

Dataset Name Description
LLaVA-OneVision-2-VideoCaption Extremely dense video captions
LLaVA-OneVision-2-Spatial 3D-aware spatial reasoning
LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-Mid-Training-85M 85M concept-balanced mid-training corpus
LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-Instruct Full instruction-tuning mixture

💡 Why it matters

The LLaVA-OneVision-2 release was noted as a next-generation multimodal model with a fully open pipeline where encoder weights, training code, configs, and full training logs are released end-to-end. This commitment to transparency allows for detailed analysis of the training processes and architectural choices, such as the integration of codec-aligned vision encoders.

item.title: RealmForge: Open-Source Platform for Persistent Swarms of LLM Agents
item.description:
RealmForge: Open-Source Platform for Persistent Swarms of LLM Agents

RealmForge is an open‑source platform that orchestrates large swarms of LLM‑powered agents within a persistent, graph‑based world.

🔍 Overview

  • Open‑source platform for orchestrating vast swarms of LLM‑powered agents, each with unique identities, goals, and evolving relationships.
  • Operates within a Structured World Model that persists across sessions.
  • Moves beyond simple chat‑based interactions to emergent narratives, economies, and simulated societies.

🧩 Architecture

  • World Conductor service manages temporal flow, advancing the simulation in tick‑based cycles.
  • Chronicler module records all events into a searchable lore database.
  • Structured World Model (SWM) is a directed graph of entities (agents, locations, objects, concepts) with properties, inventory, and narrative history.
  • Relationship Graph decays over time if not reinforced, mimicking fading memory.
  • Narrative Market where agent desires act as bids for attention; the World Conductor selects the most pressing conflict or opportunity and creates a Plot Thread.
  • Environmental Events (e.g., storm, festival, dragon sighting) are generated based on internal clocks or random rolls.

⚙️ Agent Design

  • Each agent has a Persona Script (core traits, goals, knowledge cut‑off) and a State Vector (mood, health, inventory, relationships).
  • Agents possess a Perception Radius, limiting visibility and interaction to nearby entities in the graph, creating realistic information asymmetry.
  • Agents can delegate tasks to sub‑agents, enabling recursive complexity.
  • Language‑agnostic persona system; entities store language tags, allowing multilingual interaction through diplomat agents or translation artifacts.

📈 Persistence & Emergence

  • The world is a queryable knowledge graph, not a flat text string.
  • Time advances in discrete Epochs (configurable from seconds to months of in‑world time); agents act based on schedules, task durations, and information propagation.
  • The simulation tracks resource scarcity, faction reputation, and character development over simulated days or years.

📋 Core Components

Component Role
Structured World Model Directed graph storing entities, properties, inventory, and narrative history
World Conductor Advances simulation ticks, selects Plot Threads from Narrative Market
Chronicler Records all events into a searchable lore database
Relationship Graph Tracks relationships; decays over time without reinforcement
Narrative Market Hosts agent desires as bids for attention
Environmental Event Engine Generates storms, festivals, dragon sightings, etc.

item.title: Haiku RAG Launches Open-Source Agentic Retrieval System with Docling and Ollama
item.description:
Haiku RAG Launches Open-Source Agentic Retrieval System with Docling and Ollama

A new open-source project called Haiku RAG has been released, offering an agentic retrieval-augmented generation system that answers questions about user documents with citations to page numbers and section headings. The system runs on an embedded LanceDB database with open models through Ollama by default, requiring no server or API key. It supports multiple providers via Pydantic AI, and the same database can live on S3, GCS, Azure, or LanceDB Cloud. Built on LanceDB, Pydantic AI, and Docling, it ingests PDFs, office documents, HTML, Markdown, and images. The stored DoclingDocument preserves headings, tables, pictures, and page provenance. Search utilizes hybrid vector and full-text retrieval, optional reranking with cross-encoders and various providers, section-aware context expansion, and image search with multimodal embedders. It can answer with RAG capability, searching, running sandboxed Python for counting and aggregation, and citing page numbers and headings. Vision models receive figures directly. Optional capabilities compact earlier evidence and require answers to declare grounding. Citations can be checked by drawing chunks on page images from CLI, chat TUI, or Python. Integration options include Python API, native Pydantic AI capabilities, plugin hooks, MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, and Claude Desktop, plus a reference web app. The haiku-ingester service supports filesystem, HTTP, S3, and WebDAV sources with a SQLite or Postgres job queue, control plane, dashboard, tags, rollback, vacuum, and health checks. Python 3.12 or newer is required. Installation offers two packages: pip install haiku.rag for full features including Docling, VoyageAI, Cohere embedders, all rerankers, and TUI; and pip install haiku.rag-slim for core with extras. Default configuration uses Ollama for embeddings and answers. Commands include haiku-rag init, haiku-rag add-src, haiku-rag search, haiku-rag ask, haiku-rag chat, and haiku-rag mcp --stdio. The ingester service runs separately with haiku-ingester serve and supports continuous ingestion from configured sources.

#AI #RAG #OpenSource #LLM #Docling #LanceDB

Source: ggozad/haiku.rag

item.title: Pagekin: Open-source AI novel writing app
item.description:
Pagekin: Open-source AI novel writing app

Pagekin, formerly AI Novel Writer, is a free, open-source AI novel writing app designed for long novels and web fiction. It is local-first, with no model bundled, and available for Windows and macOS. Maintained by EthanYoQ, Pagekin allows users to write and manage their works locally on their own computers.

🔍 Overview

  • Free, open-source AI novel writing app
  • Designed for long novels and web fiction
  • Local-first, no model bundled
  • Available for Windows and macOS
  • Maintained by EthanYoQ

🧩 How it works

  • Works exist on your own computer
  • Software does not bundle models; users can connect their own API Key or use Ollama to run local models
  • Supports importing novels in .txt, .md, or .epub formats
  • Architecture page is divided into four sections: story premise, character list, world view, and plot outline
  • Each character has basic settings, current status, and relationship map
  • Character cards can be pasted or imported from files
  • Blueprint page lists planned chapters
  • Batch creation allows writing up to 10 chapters at a time
  • AI uses the chapter’s blueprint, relevant characters, world view, summary of previous text, and the full text of the previous chapter
  • Text editor supports inserting two full-width spaces as paragraph indentation
  • All generation tasks are managed in the running side page, divided into ongoing, history, and diagnostic pages
  • Tracks main plot, subplots, and foreshadowing by chapter
  • Knowledge base can be imported with reference materials in .txt or .md formats
  • Export options include merged Markdown, chaptered Markdown, or TXT
  • Works can be saved locally or backed up to a WebDAV cloud service
  • Writing skills can be selected from a local folder or single SKILL.md file, or from a GitHub address
  • Available in light and dark themes
  • Supports Chinese and English interfaces
  • Supports OpenAI compatible and Gemini native protocols
  • Built-in presets for various service providers: DeepSeek, SiliconFlow, BigModel, OpenAI, xAI, Google Gemini, Ollama, NovelAI, and custom
  • Semantic search in the knowledge base requires a separate vector model, configurable in the retrieval model settings
  • Upgrades only update the application itself, preserving works, character cards, and settings
  • Supports arm64 for Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4, etc.)

🚀 Availability

  • Free, open-source
  • Windows & macOS
  • Supports arm64 for Apple Silicon Macs

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a local-first approach to AI novel writing
  • Offers flexibility in model usage and integration
  • Supports multiple export and backup options
  • Allows for detailed character and plot management
  • Supports multiple languages and themes
  • Offers a range of service provider presets
  • Ensures data privacy by keeping works and settings local
  • Preserves user data during upgrades

item.title: Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users
item.description:
Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users

Verlihub is an advanced NMDC+S protocol server for Linux and Windows operating systems. It offers a high-performance solution with low RAM and CPU usage, capable of holding more than 25,000 users.

🔍 Overview

Verlihub provides high-level functionality for managing connections, hub administration, and security features. It uses epoll on Linux and Windows, and supports worker threads for slow work to maintain performance efficiency.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resource Efficiency: Low RAM and CPU usage using epoll on both Linux and Windows operating systems.
  • Capacity: Able to hold more than 25,000 users.
  • Security: Built-in TLS-encrypted connections using OpenSSL, supporting plain and encrypted users on the same port. An external TLS proxy is also supported, sending the real address of the user with the $MyIP command.
  • Database Support: Offers backup and restore functionality for MySQL or MariaDB databases.
  • Customization and Localization: Allows extending functionality via Lua scripts (including HTTP requests) and supports hub messages in many languages.
  • User and Connection Management: Handles user management with privileges, clients and connections management, and logging of user IPs and complete MyINFOs (requires Ledokol).
  • GeoIP Integration: Tracks the GeoIP country, city, and ASN of users using MaxMindDB.
  • Statistics: Generates statistics for your hub (requires Ledokol).

🚀 Availability

Verlihub builds on Windows with MinGW-w64, with dependencies and build steps detailed in Install.md. TLS support is built-in using OpenSSL and enabled by default; to build without it, the -DUSE_TLS=OFF flag can be used.

Several resources are available for support and integration:

item.title: Kiro Crew Offers a Persistent, Self-Evolving Development Workspace
item.description:
Kiro Crew Offers a Persistent, Self-Evolving Development Workspace

Kiro Crew is an open-source development workspace that runs locally or remotely on your hardware, with work designed to persist, learn, and evolve beyond a single session.

🔍 Overview

You can work with Kiro Crew through a desktop app, web dashboard, or CLI, and continue the same work through connection tools such as Slack and Discord.

🧩 How it works

  • Multi-step tasks can run unattended.
  • Recurring jobs run on a schedule.
  • Heartbeats monitor systems until something needs attention.
  • Kiro Crew Apps adapt the workspace to a specific job, combining a purpose-built interface with agents, skills, schedules, integrations, and backend services.

⚙️ Setup and updates

Kiro Crew can be run in several ways:

  • Use the desktop app, which includes automatic updates.
  • Install it on a machine or remote host with a one-line install.
  • Use the Docker image for always-on servers.
  • Build it from source.

The default agent runs on kiro-cli, which must be installed and signed in to separately. On first launch, Kiro Crew checks for this prerequisite and links to the official setup guide if it is missing. Download links fetch the newest build on their channel, and the app updates itself on that same channel. The recommended channel is Stable unless there is a reason to choose another.

🚀 Availability

Kiro Crew is available for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Package options include:

Platform Package
macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) .dmg
Windows (x64) .exe
Linux (x86_64 or aarch64) .deb, .rpm, or AppImage

On Linux, the one-line install is the recommended starting point; a desktop package can be added for a native window and in-app updates.

An open‑source AI Security Operations Center called AiSOC has been released. It runs on‑premises, requires no external API keys, and provides end‑to‑end alert fusion, automated triage, and auditable AI‑driven investigation.

🔍 Overview

🧩 How it works

  • The platform runs 2,966 executable rules from a 7,407‑rule library to fire alerts.
  • Fired alerts are grouped into incidents and handed to an AI agent.
  • The agent’s prompts, tool calls, and reasoning are fully auditable.
  • After investigation the agent proposes a response that a human must approve.
  • New threat‑intelligence data (e.g., the CISA KEV catalog) re‑sweeps historical data, again requiring human approval before any vendor interaction.

⚙️ Key details

  • Alert fusion, LLM‑agent triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation.
  • Replayable decision ledger for every agent step.
  • MCP server ships for Claude, Cursor, and Continue.

  • Alerts show the originating connector; automated triage displays the local model’s verdict, confidence, and rationale verbatim.

Method Command
Windows PowerShell `iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beenuar/AiSOC/main/install.ps1

item.description:
Phonon: Open‑source On‑device Text‑to‑Speech Model Released

Two weeks ago, we opened up Phonon, our small text‑to‑speech model that runs on your own device.

🔍 Overview

  • Phonon runs on your own device, needs no server or network, and your typed text stays with you.
  • It works on phones, laptops, single‑board computers and in a browser tab.
  • The model was downloaded more than 200,000 times in its first two weeks and is still trending on Hugging Face.

🧩 How it works

  • Based on the Pocket TTS lineage and uses flow matching to generate audio, a technique different from other TTS systems.
  • Generates audio latents autoregressively: each step outputs a latent that becomes the next input, with training loss computed on them.
  • Training was initially numerically unstable and required several tricks to achieve quality across five languages.

⚙️ Key details

  • Two model sizes: about 65 MB and 75 MB.
  • Model variants:
Model Approx. Size License Language Coverage
Phonon 31m 65 MB Apache 2.0 (free for commercial use) English
Phonon 40m 75 MB CC BY‑NC (non‑commercial) English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese
  • Together the models support English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese.
  • More than 100 built‑in voices; additional voices can be created in Gradium Studio.
  • Handles phone numbers, dates and codes, which many TTS systems struggle with.

🚀 Performance

  • On intelligibility tests, Phonon ranks first in German and Spanish and is in the top three for every evaluated language, alongside models up to 100 × its size.
  • It tops the CPU streaming benchmark on time‑to‑first audio, highlighting its speed.
  • A new inference framework, ptts, was built for Phonon and supports more than 10 backends (CPU Intel/Arm/WebAssembly, GPU CUDA/Vulkan/Metal/WebGPU, NPU Apple Core ML/Snapdragon®).

📦 Availability

  • Phonon is included in 🤗 Transformers from version 5.21 as the reference PyTorch implementation.
  • The 31 m model (English, Apache 2.0) can be used freely in commercial products.
  • The 40 m model (five languages, CC BY‑NC) is free for non‑commercial projects; commercial use follows a pricing model based on number of users, not amount of generated speech.
  • Example use cases: on an Apple Watch with Wi‑Fi off, Phonon guides a coffee brew step‑by‑step; on an iPhone with no signal, it counts repetitions during a workout.

The community‑maintained Awesome‑Kubernetes repository has been packaged into a GitBook, allowing anyone to download and read the curated list as a book.

  • Kubernetes is known to be a descendant of Google’s system BORG.

  • Borg was built to manage both long‑running services and batch jobs, which had previously been handled by two separate systems: Babysitter and the Global Work Queue.

item.title: Microsoft releases open-source tool to boost two-to-six-week weather forecasts
item.description:
Microsoft releases open-source tool to boost two-to-six-week weather forecasts

Microsoft Research has unveiled a new machine‑learning tool that corrects systematic bias in existing weather models, extending reliable forecasts out to two‑to‑six weeks.

🔍 Overview

  • Old‑school physics‑based forecasting and current AI models lose reliability beyond two weeks, a problem Microsoft says it has solved with machine learning.
  • The tool, called Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC), is now open‑source software and its findings were published today in Nature.
  • Microsoft joins Google, Nvidia and other firms developing AI tools for weather forecasting.

🧩 How it works

  • PBC uses machine learning to identify systematic bias in a model and make corrections, rather than building a new standalone weather model.
  • It can run on standard CPUs, avoiding the supercomputer or GPU clusters required by traditional physics‑based or generative‑AI forecasts.
  • Example bias: climate‑change‑induced warming can cause a model that relies on historic records to predict temperatures that are too cold.

📊 Performance

  • Improves the accuracy of the European Centre for Medium‑Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) physics‑based model for 98 % of precipitation targets and 92 % of temperature targets.
  • Doubles the accuracy of ECMWF’s new AI forecasting system in the study’s analysis.
Model corrected by PBC Reported improvement
ECMWF physics‑based model (precipitation) 98 % of targets more accurate
ECMWF physics‑based model (temperature) 92 % of targets more accurate
ECMWF AI forecasting system Accuracy doubled

🌍 Accessibility & Impact

  • Designed as a lightweight, easy‑to‑train approach that resource‑strained weather agencies can adopt.
  • Runs on CPUs, lowering compute and infrastructure barriers that often exclude agencies in economically developing countries.
  • Aims to give farmers, emergency responders and other stakeholders more certain forecasts for planning.
  • Genevieve Flaspohler notes the method lets scientists without huge pools of resources configure models for specific localities.
  • Flaspohler’s nonprofit Rhiza Research is testing PBC with the Kenya Meteorological Service Authority, funded by the Gates Foundation, ahead of an expected extreme rainy season during a record‑breaking El Niño.

🚀 Availability

  • The software is released as open‑source, allowing the broader community to adopt the bias‑correction technique.
  • The research team includes scientists from Microsoft, MIT, ECMWF and other institutions.
  • ECMWF previously recognized the work by awarding it in its AI Weather Quest competition.
  • Matthew Chantry of ECMWF called the paper “a good example of new ideas being developed for the benefit and consideration of the community,” while noting the challenge of turning ideas into operational processes.

item.title: Mem0 Open‑Source Memory Layer Empowers AI Agents with Persistent Context
item.description:
Mem0 Open‑Source Memory Layer Empowers AI Agents with Persistent Context

Mem0 (pronounced “mem‑zero”) is an open‑source memory layer that sits between your application and an LLM such as GPT, Claude, or Llama. It filters durable facts from each interaction, stores them in a separate vector database, and injects the most relevant memories back into the prompt so the agent can answer without rereading the full chat history.

🔍 Overview

  • AI agents forget facts that fall outside the model’s context window, e.g., a customer’s name learned yesterday may be asked again today.
  • Mem0 addresses this by decoupling “memory” from the language model and managing a growing store of verified facts.

🧩 How It Works

The official README describes a three‑stage pipeline:

Stage Function
Extraction A language model reads the conversation and extracts durable facts (e.g., preferences, names, decisions).
Storage Extracted facts are stored as embeddings in a vector store with entity links (name, product, place).
Retrieval On a new query, Mem0 combines semantic search, BM25 keyword search, and entity matching, then inserts the top results into the prompt.
  • The April 2026 algorithm stores memories in a stack without overwriting older entries and records facts confirmed by the agent itself.
  • Default models are OpenAI gpt‑5‑mini for extraction and text‑embedding‑3‑small for embeddings, but any compatible model (including local ones via Ollama) can be swapped.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Licensed under Apache‑2.0.
  • 66,458 ⭐ on GitHub (as of 2 Oct 2026).
  • Developed by a Y Combinator S24 batch startup.
  • Provides an official plugin for OpenClaw; in OpenClaw it replaces the built‑in memory backend (one memory slot per agent).
  • Mem0 is not a chatbot; it is a memory layer that can be placed in front of any LLM.
  • Benchmark claims (from the Mem0 team):
    • 26 % relative improvement on LLM‑as‑a‑Judge metrics vs. OpenAI memory on the LOCOMO benchmark.
    • p95 latency 91 % lower.
    • Token usage reduced by >90 % compared to sending the full conversation.
    • Scores of 92.5 on LoCoMo and 94.4 on LongMemEval (April 2026 algorithm).
  • All benchmark numbers come from the Mem0 team, measured on a paid cloud platform with proprietary optimizations; open‑source deployments may see lower but proportional gains.

🚀 Availability

  • Distributed as a library, a self‑hosted server, or a cloud service.
  • Cloud offering includes a free tier and paid plans up to $249 per month.
  • The open‑source version is free, but users still incur indirect costs for model API calls (extraction / embedding) and for running a vector‑store server (e.g., Qdrant or PGVector).

💡 Why It Matters

  • Eliminates the need for agents to reread the entire chat history, reducing token consumption.
  • Provides long‑term, per‑user/per‑session memory that grows with interactions.
  • Lowers latency for memory‑augmented responses.
  • Offers a plug‑and‑play replacement for existing memory backends (e.g., OpenClaw) when a more scalable solution is required.

item.description:
Open‑Source RemoveMacAI Tool Deletes Apple Intelligence Models, Frees Up Storage

A new open‑source command‑line utility called RemoveMacAI lets macOS users delete Apple Intelligence models and disable its bundled AI features in a single step, reclaiming roughly a dozen gigabytes of disk space.

🔧 What RemoveMacAI Does

  • ‘RemoveMacAI’ switches off Apple’s AI features, deletes its AI models, and blocks them from being downloaded again.
  • It removes the on‑disk foundation models, which the developer says take up about 12 GB of space (some users report even more).
  • The changes persist across macOS updates.
  • Dictation continues to work after removal.
  • The tool provides a removemacai revert command to re‑enable all features and allow the models to download again.
  • A removemacai status command shows the size of each individual AI model on the Mac.

“I wrote RemoveMacAI to do all of it in one go.”

📦 Storage Impact

  • Apple Intelligence models remain on disk by default, occupying about 12 GB according to the developer.
  • A user measured 35.05 GB of space labeled “Apple Intelligence” on a MacBook Air.
  • Running RemoveMacAI deletes these models, freeing the corresponding storage.

⚙️ How It Works

  1. The tool toggles off the following AI‑related features:
    • Siri
    • Writing Tools
    • Genmoji
    • Image Playground
    • The ChatGPT extension
    • All summary functions
  2. It then deletes the stored foundation models from the file system.
  3. Finally, it prevents macOS from re‑downloading the models unless the user runs removemacai revert.

📋 Feature List

Feature Action performed by RemoveMacAI
Siri Turned off
Writing Tools Turned off
Genmoji Turned off
Image Playground Turned off
ChatGPT extension Turned off
Summaries Turned off

📆 Availability

  • The utility is open‑source and was announced by its developer on Reddit.
  • It replaces the single Settings toggle that existed for disabling Apple Intelligence before it was removed in macOS 27, where the models stayed on disk and settings were split across multiple panes (including several under Screen Time).

💡 Why It Matters

  • Users who prefer not to run Apple’s on‑device AI can now remove the models entirely, reclaiming storage without losing core functionality like Dictation.
  • The tool simplifies what previously required navigating about a dozen settings across various preference panes.
  • By blocking future downloads, it ensures the storage savings remain until the user decides to restore the features.

item.title: Ubicloud Launches Open Source Cloud for Bare Metal Providers
item.description:
Ubicloud Launches Open Source Cloud for Bare Metal Providers

Ubicloud is an open source cloud that can run anywhere, providing IaaS cloud features on bare metal providers including AWS Bare Metal, Leaseweb, and Hetzner.

🔍 Overview

Ubicloud offers an open source alternative to traditional cloud services to reduce costs and return infrastructure control to the user. The project aims to implement 10% of cloud services that account for 80% of consumption.

🧩 How it works

Ubicloud utilizes a control plane to manage a data plane that leverages open source software. The control plane is responsible for cloudifying bare metal Linux machines.

Component Technical Implementation
Elastic Compute Control plane communicates with Linux bare metal servers using SSH
Virtual Machine Monitor Cloud Hypervisor, with each instance contained in Linux namespaces
Networking IPsec tunneling for encrypted private networks
Firewalls & Load Balancers Linux nftables
Block Storage Storage Performance Development Toolkit (SPDK)

⚙️ Key details

  • Networking: Supports dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 with both public and private networking. Ubicloud assigns IPv6 addresses to VMs, or users can add IPv4 addresses leased from their provider to the control plane. Each customer’s VMs operate in their own networking namespace.
  • Storage: Non-replicated block storage is provided via SPDK, which allows for future implementation of replication and snapshots. Data encryption keys are encrypted following security best practices.
  • Access Control: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) allows for the definition of roles, attributes, and permissions for fine-grained resource access.

🚀 Availability

Users can set up Ubicloud themselves on supported providers or use a managed service. The managed cloud is approximately 3x cheaper than AWS.

CowAgent Open-Source Super AI Assistant and Agent Harness Released

CowAgent (formerly chatgpt-on-wechat) is an open-source super AI assistant and reference implementation of Agent Harness engineering designed to plan tasks, control computers and external services, and self-evolve through memory and knowledge.

🔍 Overview

CowAgent is a lightweight, extensible AI assistant that functions as a complete Agent Harness. It allows users to plug in major LLM providers and run the system 24/7 on a server or personal computer.

🧩 How it works

CowAgent utilizes a decoupled architecture where every layer is independently extensible:

  • Channels: Messages flow in through various integrated platforms.
  • Agent Core: Plans and reasons using available tools, skills, knowledge, and memory.
  • Models: Generate the response, which is then sent back through the originating channel.

  • Task Execution: Decomposes complex tasks and executes them step-by-step, looping over tools until the goal is reached.
  • Multi-Agent Teams: Supports teams of Agents with individual roles, models, skills, and knowledge collaborating in shared conversations.
  • Memory and Knowledge: Uses a three-tier architecture (context $\rightarrow$ daily $\rightarrow$ core) with hybrid keyword and vector retrieval and automatic Deep Dream distillation. It auto-curates structured knowledge into a Markdown wiki and an evolving knowledge graph.
  • Self-Evolution: Automatically reviews conversations to improve skills, follow up on unfinished tasks, and consolidate memory.
  • Tooling: Includes native MCP integration and built-in tools for file I/O, terminal, browser, scheduler, memory retrieval, and web search.

item.description:
Launch of Open-Source MCP Memory Service for AI Agents

A new open-source memory backend for AI agents has been released, providing a self-hosted service for storing decisions and sharing causal knowledge graphs.

🔍 Overview

The MCP Memory Service allows agents to capture project context, architecture decisions, and code patterns automatically. This ensures new sessions begin with existing knowledge. The service is framework-agnostic and compatible with several tools, including:

  • LangGraph
  • CrewAI
  • AutoGen
  • Claude Desktop
  • OpenCode
  • Any HTTP client

🧩 How it works

The system utilizes a knowledge graph with typed edges to track causes, fixes, and contradictions, allowing agents to share causal chains rather than just facts. Technical specifications include:

  • Local Embeddings: Run via ONNX to ensure memory stays within the user’s infrastructure.
  • Performance: Context retrieval occurs in 5ms.
  • Consolidation: Autonomous consolidation compresses old memories.
  • Real-time Updates: SSE events provide notifications when memories are stored or deleted.

⚙️ Key details

The service is licensed under Apache 2.0 and features a REST API with 76 endpoints. Key API and configuration elements include:

Feature Description
X-Agent-ID header Auto-tags memories by agent identity for scoped retrieval
conversation_id Bypasses deduplication for incremental conversation storage
REST API Runs at http://localhost:8000 without requiring an MCP client library
Interface Includes a CLI, dashboard, REST API, MCP, and OAuth

🚀 Availability

Users can install the service via pip install mcp-memory-service. Configuration paths for Claude Desktop are provided for multiple operating systems:

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json
  • Linux: ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

Command-line options include claude mcp add memory -- memory server and MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http.

💡 Why it matters

Because the service is self-hosted, it incurs zero cloud cost and avoids cloud lock-in and API costs. Memory is shared across all agents and runs.
